pillar_reactions.evidence: Payment and onboarding call only. The nearest adjacent moment is equipment guidance, where the rep sensibly held the prospect back from buying the wrong thing: 'I need to go buy a kettlebell. Is that correct?' / 'Yes, but don't do it right now. You will talk with Trevor about it. What kind of kettlebell, what kind of weight to start with.'
Not raised at any point on this call.

Not presented as a pillar. The rep did extend the personal-contact pattern seen elsewhere in this batch — 'I'm going to be in touch with you because I really love to see how are you progressing' — and set up WhatsApp as a direct escalation route for rescheduling.

anchors.raw: you didn't mention installments, you just said put it on a credit card and pay the credit card off, which, God, I didn't, it was reluctant. I think to do that, just to end up paying more interest on it.
anchors.note: The decisive anchor of the deal, and it is entirely self-inflicted. The prospect was not resisting $6,000 — he was resisting the total cost of $6,000 plus credit card interest, because that was the only funding route he had been given. His mental price was therefore higher than the actual price. The moment the rep said 'with no interest at all', the objection evaporated. This is worth generalising: on the Arturo and smanian calls the same week, interest-bearing third-party finance was the FIRST structured option offered, which manufactures this same inflated mental price.

anchors.raw: I just paid $12,000 for a new air conditioner, I have to do another $17,000 with the solar panels that I have put up and I just don't have the cash flow at this point in time.
anchors.note: Cuts both ways and the rep read it correctly. In the short term it is a hard liquidity constraint. In substance it is strong evidence of capacity — $29,000 of discretionary home investment in the same period — so the correct response was to move the payment in time rather than to discount, qualify out, or interrogate the balance sheet. He did exactly that.

unmet_demand.want: An instalment option without interest, made known at the point the price was presented
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Not a gap in the product at all — the option existed and was offered here without hesitation. It was a gap in what the prospect was told thirty minutes earlier on the paired call, where the only routes named were a credit card or interest-bearing third-party financing over twelve months. He had already decided to postpone on the basis of incomplete information and only recovered the deal by turning up to cancel.

unmet_demand.want: A self-service way to reschedule the onboarding call with Trevor if something came up
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked for it directly and the confirmation email did not contain it — 'It doesn't say anything about rescheduling, but just join instructions.' The rep improvised by adding him to his personal WhatsApp and promising the team would chase regardless. Functional, but it routes a routine scheduling task through one individual's private messaging.
